$comment: UK Extradition Law - the s.87 human-rights gateway for Part 2/Category 2 requests and the Article 8 proportionality test in Norris. Fresh research this session. Both nodes are post-2004/2010 and fetched directly, no BAILII/pre-2009 access issue to route around (Norris is a 2010 UKSC case, within Find Case Law's coverage). A statutory mismatch in the original research brief was caught and corrected during research: s.21A is a Part 1 (Category 1, EAW-style) provision, not Part 2 - s.87 is the correct Part 2 human-rights gateway paired with Norris, a USA (Part 2) case.
verification_method: Extradition Act 2003 s.87 fetched live and directly from legislation.gov.uk's in-force text, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time. Norris v Government of the United States of America [2010] UKSC 9 fetched live and directly from Find Case Law, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time, cross-checked against UK Human Rights Blog and CaseMine's independent commentary.

authorities.name: Extradition Act 2003, s.87 (Human rights, Part 2/Category 2 cases)
authorities.date_note: Date the Act came into force. The text verified this session is the current in-force (revised) version.
authorities.proposition: In a Category 2 (Part 2) extradition request, the extradition judge must decide whether the person's extradition would be compatible with the Convention rights within the meaning of the Human Rights Act 1998 (s.87(1)) - the statutory gateway through which Article 8 ECHR is litigated. If incompatible, the judge must discharge the person (s.87(2)); if compatible, the case proceeds to the Secretary of State for a decision on extradition (s.87(3)).
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly this session, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time - both fetches consistent on s.87(1)-(3)'s exact text. A related but distinct provision, s.21A (Part 1's own proportionality test, inserted 2014), was checked and correctly excluded as not applicable to this Part 2 pairing.

authorities.name: Norris v Government of the United States of America (No 2)
authorities.judge_or_panel: Lord Phillips (President), Lord Hope, Lord Rodger, Lady Hale, Lord Brown, Lord Mance, Lord Judge, Lord Collins, Lord Kerr
authorities.proposition: Establishes the leading test for when Article 8 ECHR can defeat extradition under s.87: the public interest in honouring extradition arrangements and prosecuting serious crime is very strong, and Article 8 will only outweigh it where some quite exceptionally compelling feature, or combination of features, is present. This is not a separate formal 'exceptionality' threshold test but a description of how a properly conducted proportionality assessment will, in practice, almost always come out.
authorities.verification_note: Fetched live and directly from Find Case Law this session, independently re-fetched and re-confirmed a second time - both fetches consistent on paragraph 56's exceptionally-compelling-feature test. Cross-checked against UK Human Rights Blog and CaseMine's independent commentary. A later case, H(H) v Deputy Prosecutor of the Italian Republic, Genoa [2012] UKSC 25, refines this test where children's Article 8 rights are engaged - not independently verified in this session, a candidate for a future extension node.

edges.verified_via: Norris v Government of the United States of America [2010] UKSC 9, para 56, fetched directly from Find Case Law and independently re-confirmed: supplies the operative proportionality test for the s.87 human-rights compatibility question.

what_this_is_not: Two verified nodes covering the Article 8 proportionality test for Part 2 extradition requests. Does not cover Part 1 (European Arrest Warrant-style) requests, the s.21A statutory proportionality test, the bars to extradition beyond human rights (double jeopardy, passage of time, extraneous considerations), children's Article 8 rights specifically (see H(H), not independently verified), or any other Extradition Law subject - all remain unbuilt.
